html:
A Finn Dorset sheep born on 5 July 1996 at the Roslin Institute near Edinburgh, Scotland: the first mammal cloned from an adult body cell.

Ian Wilmut, Keith Campbell and their team took a cell from the udder of a six year old ewe, moved its nucleus into an egg cell whose own nucleus had been removed, and grew the result in a surrogate mother. Most attempts failed; Dolly was the one lamb from 277 tries. She was named after the singer Dolly Parton.

Her birth was announced in February 1997 and caused a stir. Scientists had thought adult cells could not be turned back to make a whole new animal. Politicians rushed to ban human cloning. The work fed into research on stem cells and on reprogramming cells, the line of biology that began with the DNA double helix. Dolly had six lambs and was put down in 2003 with a lung disease.
sum: A Finn Dorset sheep born on 5 July 1996 at the Roslin Institute near Edinburgh, Scotland: the first mammal cloned from an adult body cell.
